एलक: Elaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 12, 2.
एलपत्र: Elapatra: A mythical serpent living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7. [See Elāpatra]
एलापत्र: Elāpatra m.: A mythical serpent. A. Son of Kadrū 1. 31. 6, 2. B He told serpents what he heard when he crawled into the lap of his mother when the curse was pronounced by her; Brahmā had told the gods the remedy partially to avoid the effect of the curse; he therefore advised Vāsuki to give his sister Jaratkāru to give in marriage to sage Jaratkāru; their son would stop the sacrifice of snakes 1. 34. 1-18; his advice was received with joy by serpents 1. 35. 1; Brahmā informed gods that what Elāpatra had told the snakes was exactly what he had in mind; Elāpatra's advice was to the advantage of the serpents and that it would prove true 1. 35. 8, 11. C. Elāpatra's observation on life: One who is struck by fate takes recourse to fate since he finds no other way out (दैवेनोपहतो राजन् यो भवेद् इह पूरुषः । स दैवम् एवाश्रयते नान्यत् तत्र परायणम् 1. 34. 3). [See Elapatra.]
एकपर्वतक: Ekaparvataka m.: Name of a mountain. Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna, while pro-ceeding to Magadha, crossed the rivers flowing near the mountain Ekaparvataka 2. 18. 27.
एकरात्र: Ekarātra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is controlled (नियतः) and speaks the truth, if he spends one night (एक-रात्रोषितः) at this तीर्थ (which explains its name), he is glorified in the world of Brahman (ब्रह्मलोके महीयते) 3. 81. 159.
एकहंस: Ekahaṃsa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing at Ekahaṃsa one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows (गोसहस्र-फलं लभेत्) 3. 81. 16.
एकचक्रा: Ekacakrā f.: Name of a town. A. Description: Delightful (रम्य) 1. 156. 3; (रमणीय) 1. 144. 11; whole-some (निरामय) 1. 144. 11; many pleas-ing forests and gardens around Ekacakrā (यानीह रमणीयानि वनान्य् उपवनानि च) 1. 156. 4. B. Epic events: (1) Vyāsa advised the Pāṇḍavas to live in the town Ekacakrā concealing their identity (वस-तेह प्रतिच्छन्नाः); Vyāsa then went with them to Ekacakrā and put Kunti and her sons in the house of a Brāhmaṇa 1. 144. 12, 18; he asked them to live there until he returned to the town (इह मां संप्रतीक्षध्वम् आगमिष्याम्य् अहं पु-नः) 1. 144. 19; (ममागमनकांक्षिणः) 1. 144. 11; (2) The Pāṇḍavas went to Ekacakrā and lived for some time in the house of a Brāhmaṇa (एकचक्रां गतास् ते तु) 1. 145. 1-2; (3) When some people heard about the death of Baka, they went out of the town next morning and saw the Rākṣasa dead on the ground; then they re-turned to Ekacakrā and reported the news to others 1. 152. 8-9; the people of the entire country flocked to Ekacakrā (not named) to see the most wonderful event (ततो जानपदाः सर्वे आजग्मुर् नगरं प्रति । तम् अद्भुतं द्रष्टुम्) 1. 152. 19; (4) The Pāṇḍavas continued to live in Ekacakrā after the death of Baka (पा-र्थास् तत्रैव चावसन्) 1. 152. 19; Kuntī once told her sons that they had lived too long in the house of the Brāhmaṇa in Ekacakrā (not named) (चिररात्रोषिताः स्मेह ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने) 1. 156. 2; as promised, Vyāsa arrived to meet the Pāṇḍa-vas living in disguise at Ekacakrā; he advised them to go to the Pāñcāla country 1. 157. 1, 16; (5) The Pāṇḍavas took leave of the Brāhmaṇa and left Ekacakrā for the town of Drupada in the Pāñcāla coun-try (ततो आमन्त्र्य तं विप्रम् … प्रतस्थे नगरिम् रम्याम् द्रुपदस्य महात्मनः) 1. 156. 6-11; (7) On way to the Pāñcāla country Yudhiṣṭhira told the Brāhmaṇas that they had come from Ekacakrā (आगतान् एकचक्रायाः) 1. 175. 4; (7) The event of the Pāṇḍavas' stay, along with Kuntī, in the house of a Brāhmaṇa in Ekacakrā, the killing of Baka, and their proceeding to the Pāñcāla country, is referred to by different persons on different occasions: (a) By Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary of the epic events told to king Janamejaya (ते वीरा एकचक्रां व्रजंस् तदा । … बकं हत्वा महाबलम् । … जग्मुः पाञ्चालानां पुरं ततः) 1. 55. 20-21; 1. 90. 79-80; (b) By Draupadī to Kṛṣṇa while recount-ing past events in the life of the Pāṇḍavas (ततश् च प्राद्रवन् सर्वे … एकचक्राम् अभिमुखाः) 3. 13. 98-99; (c) By Kṛṣṇa while addressing Duryodhana (ऊषुश् च सुचिरं कालं प्रच्छन्नाः पाण्डवास् तदा ।  … एकचक्रायाम्) 5. 126. 14.
एकपाद: Ekapāda(ka) m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: In the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणभि-मुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (प्रायाद् … दक्षि-णां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37. B. Description: Living in forests (वनवासिनः) 2. 28. 47. C. Epic events: (1) Mentioned among those whom Sahadeva subjugated in his expedition to the south before the Raja-sūya and made them pay tribute just by sending messengers (एकपादांश् च पुरुषान्  … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदा-पयत्) 2. 28. 47; (2) When they arrived for the Rājasūya they were stopped at the gate and were not allowed to enter; as tri-bute, they brought with them precious gold and silver as also forest-bred, very swift horses having different colours and there-fore looking like fire-flies, others having the colour of parrots, or resembling rainbows, or twilight clouds (एकपादांश् च … द्वारि वारितान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्-यं रजतं बहु ॥ इन्द्रगोपकवर्णाभाञ् शुकवर्णान् मनोजवान् । तथैवेन्द्रायु-धनिभान् संध्याभ्रसदृशान् अपि ॥ अनेक-वर्णान् आरण्यान् गृहीत्वाश्वान् मनोजवान् । जातरूपम् अनर्घ्यं च ददुस् तस्यैक-पादकाः ॥ ) 2. 47. 16-18.
एकपृष्ठ: Ekapṛṣṭha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; also called Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68; (एकपृष्ठा युगन्-धराः) 6. 10. 40.
एकाशनाज्योह: Ekāśanājyoha m. (pl.): Name of a people ? (Or do we separate the names as Ekāśana and Jyoha ?) A. Location: Between the mountains Meru and Mandara and along the river Śailodā; they enjoyed the delightful shade of bamboos and reeds (मेरुमन्दरयोर् मध्ये शैलोदाम् अभितो नदीम् । ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्याम् उपासते) 2. 48. 2. B. Characterization: They are described as mountaineers (एकाशनाज्योहाः  … पार्वतीयाः) 2. 48. 3, 7. C. Epic events: Their kings brought as tribute for the Rājasūya gold called पिपीलिक, given as boon by ants (?), in heaps to be measured by द्रोणस्, best black chowries and other chowries white like the moon, sweet honey from Himalayan flowers, garlands of flowers brought down by waters from the Uttara Kurus, and powerful herbs from northern Kailāsa; they were halted at the gate (एका-शनाज्योहाः … ते वै पिपिलिकं नाम वरद-त्तं पिपीलिकैः । जातरूपं द्रोणमेयम् अहार्षुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः ॥ … अजातशत्रोर् नृपतेर् द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 48. 3-7.
